newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England sees no need for dramatic rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England sees no need for dramatic rate rise.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Thursday he saw no need for a dramatic increase in British interest rates, but he did not rule out a rise before the general election.
"We don't see an urgent need for a dramatic step," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee.
But when asked if this meant he expected no rate rise before the general election he said, "I certainly wouldn't go that far".
A general election must be held by next May.

Most City economists expect George to call for higher interest rates when he meets Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke next week, although most expect the cost of borrowing to stay on hold at 6.0 percent until the end of the year.

Asked by the Committee if he thought policymakers were "ahead of the game" on monetary policy, George replied: "I think we were up with the game at the point when we raised interest rates in October."
Clarke agreed to George's request for a rate rise on October 30 and pushed up base rates by a quarter-point.

"I would simply stand on the statement we made subsequently to that, which was that some further rate rise would be required at some point in order to give us a better than even chance of achieving the inflation target."
George told the committee he did not expect to see a repetition of the 1980s runaway economic boom.
Britain was on the verge of an economic upswing but "not an 80s-type boom," he said.
